_about: Gaps in the June 2019 workbook, filled in Nov 2026 (written in David's style, for him to check). Applied by scripts/extract.py on top of the workbook. Scores are in workbook order: charisma (1-10), spontaneity, emotional savvy, sexual adventurousness, motivation, creativity, humour, spirituality, leadership, generosity (1-5).

F:Debora.note: Only charisma and spontaneity were scored; the other eight added

M:Preston.note: Common/unusual was blank; set to unusual per Ian

F:Amalia.description: Amalia is the quiet one at the end of the table who has already read the menu twice and worked out the bill. She doesn't do small talk and she doesn't do fuss, which some mistake for coldness. It isn't. Ask her about whatever she's obsessed with this year (orchids, Byzantine coins, the hydration of sourdough) and you'll get an hour of fascinating detail. Just don't expect her to laugh at your jokes. She heard them. She simply didn't think they were funny.

F:Ayanah.description: Ayanah moves through life like a cat through a sunny house: unhurried, self-contained and faintly mysterious. Ambition isn't really her thing. She would rather lie on the grass working out why clouds look the way they do than climb anybody's ladder. There's a quiet streak of the mystic about her, and she probably owns a deck of tarot cards she insists is 'just for fun'. Don't rush her. She'll get there, wherever there turns out to be.

M:Guillermo.description: Guillermo arrives like a three-piece band on a Saturday night: loud, colourful and impossible to ignore. He paints, he cooks, he plays the guitar badly but with tremendous conviction, and he has strong opinions about all three. He is not a natural leader (he'd rather you just did it his way, without the meetings), but he is generous with his laughter and his wine. Argue with him at your peril, then hug him at the end of the night. He'll have forgotten all about it.

M:Winnie.description: Usually short for Winston or Edwin, Winnie is the bloke who turns a trip to the hardware store into a three-hour adventure that somehow ends at the beach. He is charming, ridiculous and almost entirely unplanned, and people love him for it. Responsibility? He's heard of it. Give him a barbecue, a crowd and a story to tell and he is in his element. Just don't lend him your car. You'll get it back, eventually, with sand in it.
